text: The solar array on the roof produces 4.2 kW at noon and feeds the microgrid battery bank.
Battery maintenance requires checking electrolyte levels monthly and torquing terminals to 12 Nm.
The backup wind turbine cuts in at 3.5 m/s wind speed and furls automatically above 25 m/s.
The micro-hydro intake screen must be cleared of leaves after storms to keep 2.1 kW output.
Grid tie inverters synchronize phase within 2 degrees before closing the transfer relay.
The transfer switch isolates the house from the utility grid during islanding events.
Net metering credits accumulate in summer and offset winter consumption at retail rates.
Arc-flash rated gloves are required for any work on the combiner box bus bars.
The well pump is the largest single load at 1.8 kW and runs on a soft starter.
Expansion plans add 6 kW of panels and a second battery string in the coming year.
